checks_performed: Read only the authorized source JSON and draft JSON; used no web or other research files.

Reconstructed the radius-one edit characterization, deletion normal form, separator argument, dissociation-set obstruction, greedy invariant, local-cut construction, dense construction, and W_a arguments directly from definitions.

Created and ran an integer-only exhaustive checker over every labeled graph of orders 0, 3, and 6. It checked 32,768 six-vertex graphs, 2,490,368 six-vertex matching edits, 2,097,152 six-vertex separator choices, 409,548 qualifying dissociation deletions, 159,524 qualifying subcubic-cut constructions, and 1,336 dense constructions.

The checker also tested W_a for a=2,3,4, exhaustively checked all 232 matchings of K_7, and verified the stated order, triangle-support graph, factor obstruction, dissociation number, and separator values. Checker SHA-256: 52898b61e33a0592f7b0fbdd5bfe0691bbfde3430cc10b02bb409087f2e951b9.

Independently checked strict inequalities, divisibility boundaries, empty-graph behavior, polynomial termination, and the distinction between partial sufficient branches and a complete solution of the target.

claims.claim: A graph G has a radius-one neighbor with a triangle partition if and only if V(G) has a partition into triples each spanning at least two edges of G; moreover, a positive output may use additions only.
claims.evidence: If H is within radius one, E(G) symmetric-difference E(H) is a matching. In any H-triangle, two edges absent from G would share a vertex, contradicting that matching property; hence every factor triple spans at least two G-edges. Conversely, add the sole missing edge of each deficient triple. The triples are disjoint, so these additions form a matching and create the required triangle partition.
claims.search_method: Definition-level proof plus exhaustive enumeration of all graphs of orders 0, 3, and 6 and all matching edits.

claims.claim: Every radius-one negative output can be replaced by one obtained solely by deleting a matching from G.
claims.evidence: Write the edit matching as deleted edges D and added edges A. Then H0=G-D=H-A is a subgraph of H and D is a matching. A triangle partition of H0 would also be one of H, so negativity of H implies negativity of H0. Thus additions can always be discarded.
claims.search_method: Monotonicity proof plus exhaustive checking of every matching edit for all graphs through order 6.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable modulo-three separator certificate for negative outputs.
claims.evidence: Every edge of a factor triangle lies in T(H). Hence one factor triangle cannot meet two distinct components of T(H)-X: its non-X vertices would be joined in T(H). A component whose order is nonzero modulo three must have a factor triangle crossing into X, since internal factor triangles cover a multiple of three vertices. Distinct bad components require distinct disjoint crossing triangles, each consuming an X-vertex, so q≤|X| for every triangle partition. Therefore q>|X| is a sound certificate. Triangle enumeration, components, q, and a proposed matching deletion are polynomially checkable.
claims.search_method: Direct injection-and-divisibility proof plus exhaustive testing of every graph and every X through order 6.

claims.claim: If S⊆V satisfies |S|>n/3 and Δ(G[S])≤1, then a valid negative output is constructible in polynomial time from S.
claims.evidence: D=E(G[S]) is a matching. Deleting D makes S independent, so every remaining triangle contains at most one S-vertex. A partition into n/3 triangles could cover at most n/3 vertices of S, contradicting |S|>n/3. The deletion and verification are polynomial.
claims.search_method: Direct counting proof plus exhaustive testing of every candidate S through order 6.

claims.claim: A greedy polynomial algorithm resolves every input except possibly when it leaves between 1 and n/3 vertices.
claims.evidence: Each iteration removes a vertex and two current neighbors, producing a disjoint triple with at least two original G-edges. Termination means the remainder R has maximum degree at most one, and |R| is divisible by three. If R is empty, the removed triples yield the addition-only positive construction. If |R|>n/3, R satisfies claim 3 and yields a negative construction. The loop has at most n/3 iterations, so the only unhandled outcome is 0<|R|≤n/3.
claims.search_method: Invariant and termination proof plus deterministic greedy runs on every graph through order 6.

claims.claim: Given X with |X|<n/3 and Δ(G-X)≤3, a valid negative output can be constructed in polynomial time. Consequently this applies whenever fewer than n/3 vertices of G have degree at least four.
claims.evidence: Repeatedly flip a vertex across a cut of G-X whenever it has more same-side than opposite-side neighbors. Each flip increases the integer cut size, so there are at most |E(G-X)| flips. At termination, same-side degree is at most half the total degree and hence at most one when the total is at most three. Thus all monochromatic edges form a matching D. In G-D, the graph outside X is bipartite and triangle-free, so every triangle meets X. A triangle partition would require n/3 distinct X-vertices, contrary to |X|<n/3. Taking X as the vertices of G-degree at least four gives the consequence because every remaining vertex then has residual degree at most three.
claims.search_method: Exact local-cut potential proof plus exhaustive checking of every qualifying pair (G,X) through order 6.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially recognizable dense-side condition producing a positive output.
claims.evidence: Under the stated condition, a matching saturating two clones of each c∈C assigns two distinct L-neighbors to every c, giving disjoint triples with two centered edges. Exactly n-3|C| unused L-vertices remain, a nonnegative multiple of three. Every L-vertex has at most one nonneighbor, so an L-triple cannot miss two edges, since two edges of a three-vertex set share a vertex. Arbitrary unused-L triples therefore span at least two edges. Adding at most one missing edge per disjoint triple is a matching. Clone saturation is recognizable by polynomial-time bipartite matching.
claims.search_method: Constructive matching proof plus exhaustive recognition and construction on every graph through order 6.

claims.claim: The complete target is solvable for n=0,3,6.
claims.evidence: For n=0, the unchanged empty graph and empty partition suffice. For n=3 or 6, the greedy remainder has size divisible by three. If nonempty it has at least three vertices, which is strictly greater than n/3 (respectively one or two), so the negative branch applies; if empty, the positive branch applies. Exhaustive checking covered all 1, 8, and 32,768 labeled graphs at these orders.
claims.search_method: Complete case proof and exhaustive enumeration of all labeled graphs for n=0,3,6.

claims.claim: For every integer a≥2 there is a connected, triangle-support-connected graph W_a of order 3(5a+2) having no P3/triangle factor although its largest induced subgraph of maximum degree one has only 10<n/3 vertices.
claims.evidence: The construction has order 1+5(3a+1)=3(5a+2) and is connected through z. A good triple avoiding z must lie in one clique. The unique factor triple containing z touches at most two cliques, leaving at least three whole cliques of order 3a+1 to be covered internally, impossible modulo three. A maximum-degree-one induced set containing z has size at most two; one avoiding z uses at most two vertices from each clique, and two from each achieves 10. Since n/3=5a+2≥12, the inequality is strict. Every clique edge is triangle-supported, and each z-edge is supported using another vertex of its clique, so the triangle-support graph equals W_a and is connected.
claims.search_method: Symbolic proof for arbitrary a≥2, supplemented by exact checks for a=2,3,4 and exact count-vector optimization of the dissociation number.

claims.claim: The family W_a also shows that restricting the negative branch to making the graph triangle-free by a matching deletion is insufficient, while the separator certificate detects its negative answer.
claims.evidence: For any matching deletion, its restriction to a clique C_i is a matching. Partition the clique vertices into deleted-edge pairs and unmatched singletons; because |C_i|=3a+1≥7, there are at least four blocks. Choosing one vertex from each of three blocks gives a surviving triangle, so no matching deletion makes W_a triangle-free. With the empty deletion and X={z}, T(W_a)-X consists of five components of order 3a+1≡1 mod 3. Thus q=5>|X|=1, and the separator certificate proves the negative answer.
claims.search_method: General block-selection proof, exhaustive checking of all 232 matchings of K_7, and exact separator checks on W_a for a=2,3,4.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for a polynomial-time solution on every graph, or a rigorous disproof of that exact FP-membership claim. The draft supplies correct normal forms, several sufficient positive and negative branches, complete algorithms only for n=0,3,6, and an infinite family refuting two narrower strategies. It neither proves that its branches cover all graphs nor proves that the target is outside FP; indeed, its final writeup explicitly says the general FP claim remains unresolved. These are material but incomplete advances, so target coverage is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS. Because claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and the final writeup makes no full-resolution assertion, that claimed resolution is ACCURATE.
